questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to shake them.
Alert the local police.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Allow them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster is dangerous because they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should turn their heads to look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can catch the attention of other drivers by turning their heads.
Mirrors are not really helpful.
They should try to make eye contact with surrounding drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Maintain an adequate following distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To allow you time and space to identify and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
To allow for traffic counters to accurately count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To allow you time and space to identify and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance gives you time and space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road like potholes.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen by them. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Usually a good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass.
Ignore the tailgater.
Call the police.
Speed up until there is distance between your motorcycle and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up is dangerous because they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: A motorcycle usually requires:

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
A complete overhaul before every ride.
Special fuel to ensure smooth operation.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more attention than cars and trucks. Small problems on a motorcycle are much more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is discouraged.
Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: When it comes to motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Conduct a pre-ride inspection before every ride.
Conduct a pre-ride inspection each month.
Conduct a pre-ride inspection twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conduct a pre-ride inspection before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Do a thorough pre-ride inspection of your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of being involved in an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within a foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Wear dark clothing.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be prepared to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be prepared to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your turn signals and brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Clothes made from synthetic materials
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear clothes that help other drivers see you and your motorcycle. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for others to notice you on the road.

questions.question: What is important to remember about motorcycles in traffic?

options.text: They are too small to have blind spots.
Their blind spots are too small to cause problems.
They have blind spots that require you to check by looking over your shoulder.
They have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have blind spots that require you to check by looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How do you achieve the best straight-line braking?

options.text: Apply both brakes firmly without locking the wheels.
Use only the front brake and lock the front wheel.
Use the emergency brake and lock the rear wheel.
Lock both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes firmly without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: The best braking happens when you use both the front and rear brakes firmly without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks remain in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since drinking from the total drinks consumed. In this case, about four drinks would remain in the body.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to familiarize yourself with it first.
Skip the pre-ride inspection if the owner says it is in good condition.
Spend a few minutes finding all the controls before you ride.
Check that the paint is in good condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes finding all the controls before you ride.
questions.explanation: Always do the same checks on an unfamiliar motorcycle that you do on your own. Take time to locate all controls before riding because every motorcycle is different.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid sudden movements.
Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes if you need to stop, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these may have less grip than other surfaces.

questions.question: If you have been drinking and wait one hour per drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Some effects of the alcohol may still be present.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some effects of the alcohol may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system, and your abilities and judgment can still be impaired even if you wait.

questions.question: What type of pants provide the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Pants made of soft material
Pants made of heavy material
Pants that are loose and flap in the wind
Short pants that expose part of the legs

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of heavy material
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Pants should fit snug enough not to flap in the wind, but not so tight that they restrict your movement.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals to show you are turning or stopping. When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to get a better grip on the handlebars.
Not be worn because they make it harder to use the controls.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to get a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of another strong material. They give you a better grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are unsafe for motorcycles. Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare on the road.
Look ahead but try not to look for dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead of your motorcycle to spot dangers early. This helps you react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is like:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Speeding up.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting your motorcycle to a lower gear slows you down like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What helps reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?

options.text: Riding on the shoulder
Riding below the speed limit
Wearing a helmet
Not carrying a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.
